newsitem.title: SPAIN: Iberdrola's Coelba win boosts Latam drive.
newsitem.headline: Iberdrola's Coelba win boosts Latam drive.

text.p: A consortium led by Iberdrola won a controlling stake in Brazilian power distributor Coelba for $1.6 billion on Thursday, boosting the Spanish utility's plans to compete in Latin America.

"This is a big company and wonderful news," said Ramon Forcada, utilities analyst at Ibersecurities in Madrid. "Internationalisation has been one of Iberdrola's pending assignments...This is a very important step forward."

The consortium, which also includes Brazil's largest pension fund Previ and Banco do Brazil's brokerage arm BB DTVM, beat out four other offers for the 65.64 percent stake of Coelba voting capital, bidding 77.3 percent above the minimum price.
Although details on the deal were scant, analysts said the award put Iberdrola's international expansion plans in a new league and would likely put it under little strain financially.

Initially, it was not disclosed what Iberdrola's stake in the consortium was and what its costs were, but analysts said the deal was clearly its most important to date in Latin America and would put it on a better competitive footing.

Iberdrola, Spain's second-largest utility, has been making headway in Latin America, and earlier this month another consortium in which it took part won a controlling stake in Rio de Janeiro state gas company CEG and piped gas distributor Riogas.
But this deal for 1.73 billion reais dwarfs that one, which was 622.2 million reais.
Nevertheless, Iberdrola still remains well behind Spanish market leader Endesa in the race abroad, although it beat an Endesa consortium this time around.

"Strategically, it's good news...They are not as active as Endesa (in Latin America) -- they started later -- but they have been looking around," said Fabian Ramon, utilities analyst at Ahorro Corporacion Financiera.
Faced with overcapacity in a mature Spanish market, utilities must look abroad for growth. Latin America, and Brazil in particular, offer just that.
"It's a good deal. It's good to diversify, especially in Brazil," another Madrid-based analyst said.
Coelba, owned by the Brazilian state of Bahia, operates in that impoverished northern Brazilian state.
Despite the size of the deal, the cost should not overly burden Iberdrola, which has large cashflow, one analyst said.
Shares bucked the market downtrend after the news, rising 15 pesetas a share, or 0.88 percent, to 1,725 pesetas while the overall market dropped 57.43 points, or 0.84 percent, to 6,810.89.
